newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain considering spending cut not freeze for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain considering spending cut not freeze for 1997.

text.p: The Spanish government is considering cutting 1997 spending by one percent in real terms instead of simply freezing it, an Economy Ministry spokesman said.
Until now it had said spending would rise 2.6 percent in nominal terms, in line with the inflation forecast for 1997, or zero in real terms.
"The government is working on a budget based on a 1.5 percent rise in nominal spending," the spokesman said.
He was confirming earlier remarks made by budget office director Jose Barea, implying a fall of around one percent in spending in real terms.
The conservative Popular Party government has said it will maintain the major elements of social security spending and has promised repeatedly not to cut pensions for existing pensioners.

Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato has said previously he expects revenues to rise 6.0 percent next year and until recently had accompanied this with a 2.6 percent rise in nominal spending to reduce the overall public sector deficit to 3.0 percent of GDP next year from an expected 4.4 percent this year.
The draft budget, widely seen as the nearly four month old government's first real test, has to be presented to parliament by the end of September.
It will need the support of the Catalan nationalists if it is to be approved and Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar is due to meet Catalan President Jordi Pujol sometime this week to discuss the budget.
